newsitem.title: UK: Kroto "overwhelmed" to receive Nobel Prize.
newsitem.headline: Kroto "overwhelmed" to receive Nobel Prize.

text.p: Britain's Sir Harold Kroto on Wednesday said he was "totally overwhelmed" by the news he had won the 1996 Nobel Prize for Chemistry for his discovery of new forms of carbon.

"This is the greatest day of my life. It's fantastic. I'm about to have my first glass of champagne," he told Reuters by telephone from his office in the University of Sussex in southern England. He shared the prize with two U.S. scientists.
Curl, born in 1933 in Alice, Texas, has been a professor at Rice University, Houston, since 1967. Smalley, born in 1943 in Akran, Ohio, is a professor of chemistry and physics at the same university.
Kroto, born in 1939 in Wisbech, eastern England, is a professor of chemistry at the University of Sussex, in the southern English town of Brighton.

The three men discovered the fullerenes over an 11-day period in 1985 and the discovery has given to a new chemistry. "The element carbon had thus assumed an almost infinite number of different structures," the academy said.

The structure, shaped like a football, was called the "Buckminsterfullerene" after U.S. architect R. Buckminster Fuller, for his design of the geodesic dome at the 1967 Montreal World Expo. The dome closely resembles the chemical structure.
